newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Oct 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Dutch postal and telecommunications group KPN included a provision in the Part A takeover statement for TNT Ltd which effectively prevents anyone from making a counter-offer over the next three months. The provision prevents another bidder from securing one of the key assets in the transport conglomerate, its 50 per cent stake in GD Express Worldwide. Page 1.

The Kerry Packer-based Optus Vision is under two separate legal attacks from Rupert Murdoch's News Corp, Telstra and the Seven Network. Seven will tell the Supreme Court today that Packer's interests have been unfairly favoured ahead of the Network, while News and Telstra are trying to exploit the recent alliance between Optus Vision and Australis Media to break out of a contract to pay Australis A$4.5 billion over the next 25 years for programming. Page 5.

Premier Investments chief executive Harry Cooper and lawyer Monica Vinson are now seeking exemplary damages from the Australian Securities Commission and retailer Coles Myer Ltd after the ASC handed confidential documents containing Cooper and Vinson's evidence to the Yannon inquiry over to Coles. The Federal Court in Melbourne yesterday heard that the pair was due damages "on the basis that their rights have been deliberately invaded". Page 33.

Jupiters Ltd chairman Lawrie Willett told shareholders at the annual general meeting yesterday that the tax rate reduction on premier players, down from 20 per cent to 10 per cent, was helping to boost trading, with September quarter trading at both the Gold Coast Jupiters casino and Brisbane Treasury casino ahead of the same period last year. Page 34.

RTZ-CRA is expected to settle today substantial parts of its A$1.73 billion joint-venture with Freeport McMoran Inc, in a deal which gives RTZ-CRA a 40 per cent stake in any expansion of the giant Grasberg copper project in Irian Jaya. The mining giant has also set up a new company, RTZ-CRA Indonesia, to hold its interests in the Freeport-operated mine and exploration leases. Page 34.

Breakwater Island Trust will face opposition from shareholders over the proposal to surrender its North Queensland keno rights to major shareholder Jupiters Ltd at its annual meeting on Monday. Shareholders are angry that Breakwater has not offered enough information for unit holders to assess whether the deal is a good one for the trust. Page 34.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A sacked executive of oil and gas group Santos Ltd, has launched a A$O.89 million legal action against Santos and its managing director Ross Adler, and two other senior managers, alleging they conspired to remove him from the company's UK office. Page 23.

The Finance Sector Union claims it will fight any attempts of a major bank merger which may occur as an outcome of the Wallis inquiry. The FSU believes a major bank merger would cause 20,000 job losses across the industry, and has pledged to mobilise its 10,000 members to scuttle any mega-bank plans. Page 23.

The National Competition Council will launch an inquiry into Australia Post which is expected to include a review of competition limits in the domestic mail market. Currently Australia Post has a monopoly on mail costing up to A$1.80 and weighing less than 250 grams. Page 23.

The Bank of Queensland Board can expect a reshuffle at its annual meeting after thwarting State Government plans to transfer Suncorp's 44.5 per cent stake to the Metway Bank Ltd. BoQ's Neil Roberts remains confident a damaging public brawl with the Government could be avoided and a compromise could be reached with Premier Rob Borbidge, in meetings over State board seats. Page 23.

Newspaper Group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd will aim to raise A$400 million in its first entrance into the Australian debt market - a move which saw the 160-year-old publisher receive a BBB+ rating from credit agency Standard & Poor's. Page 25.

The Federal Court has granted the Australian Securities Commission an extension of the freeze on some profits from suspect TNT Ltd trading until at least November 8, even though the ASC has still not come up with any evidence that anything illegal occurred in the lead-up to last week's A$2 billion takeover bid. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The appointments of Brierley Investments' chief executive Paul Collins and Myer family member Martin Myer as members of the Coles Myer board are expected to be confirmed soon, as Coles' largest shareholder, Solomon Lew, moves to retain his influence over Coles. Brierley has built up a seven per cent stake in Coles and the Myer family has a similar share. Page 25.

Plutonic Resources yesterday announced a gold discovery of at least 250,000 ounces close to its existing Darlot project at the southern extreme of Western Australia's Yandal belt. The discovery could contain more than 500,000 ounces of gold, making it on of the richest local discoveries this decade. Page 25.

The Australian Securities Commission yesterday won an extension of freezing orders over a A$2 million paper profit made by Mark Booth from trading in TNT call options in the lead-up to last week's A$2 billion takeover bid for TNT by Dutch group KPN and although the ASC has so far been unable to contact Booth, stockbroker Ord Minnett reported that their client had contacted them by letter, instructing them to cooperate with the ASC in every way. Page 25.

Pay-TV operator Foxtel has warned Australis Media that it will launch legal action over what it sees as a breach of a heads of agreement signed in 1995 in which Australis agreed not to sell any satellite facilities. Foxtel is claiming that by agreeing to sell satellite assets into a joint venture with Optus Vision, Australis will breach the pact. Page 27.

According to an Australian Bureau of Statistics survey, the total number of dwellings financed in August rose by 0.8 per cent seasonally adjusted, following a 16 per cent surge in July. Master Builders Australia national director Wilhelm Harnisch said the result was disappointing and showed the housing market remained soft. Page 27.

Businesses employing up to 19 people spent, on average, 832 hours a year on financial accounts, invoices, tax and other compliance matters, according to the Yellow Pages Small Business Index, commissioned by the Small Business Deregulation Taskforce. Page 27.
THE AGE

Among Coles Myer's three largest shareholders, Brierley Investments chief executive Paul Collins and Myer family member Martin Myer are believed to have been offered seats on the retailer's board. BIL has built up a seven per cent stake in Coles since the Yannon affair and the Myer family has a similar stake after Coles' acquisition of the Myer Emporium in the mid-1980s. Page C1.

Plutonic Resources' shares rose 35 cents yesterday to finish at A$5.45 on the back of news that Plutonic had discovered an underground gold resource of about 250,000 ounces close to its existing Darlot project at the southern extreme of Western Australia' Yandal belt. Plutonic general manager corporate affairs Denis Clarke said the discovery was blind and appears to be in a different geological setting to the Darlot deposit. Page C1.

The Yellow Pages Small Business Index has found that small businesses spend almost a month a year on Government paperwork and compliance. The survey also revealed that one-third of small business operators considered the time spent on tax compliance excessive and one-quarter believed the time needed to complete the superannuation guarantee levy properly was excessive. Page C1.

Australia's first Islamic financing group, the Muslim Community Cooperative (Australia), wants to become a credit union to offer its members more services, but it does not want to perform a credit union's key function - lending. According to Islamic law, charging or receiving interest is prohibited, therefore loans are not permitted. Page C3.

After receiving advice from independent experts Grant Samuel & Associates that the revised bid was neither fair nor reasonable, Joe White Maltings last night said that a majority of the group's shareholders would reject the Ridley Corporation's A$98 million takeover bid. Page C3.

Stockbroker Ord Minnett last night revealed it had received a letter from mystery man Mark Booth, concerning the Australian Securities Commission's investigation into unusual trading in TNT securities. Booth instructed Ord to cooperate fully with the investigation, although the ASC has been unable to contact him since launching the examination last Thursday. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
